correctness.rationale: For the stated linear directed counts and fixed k copies, the largest label is contiguous; its observed neighbors uniquely determine the deletion update. Fixed row and column deficits recover the endpoints, so every reduced realization admits exactly one compatible endpoint insertion or exactly the reduced count of the specified internal pair. Insertion and deletion are inverse, also when the neighbors coincide. The realizability procedure inverts every accepted chain, and rejects a negative count, invalid largest-label pattern, or mismatched boundary. If an oriented pair ab with a!=b occurred twice, some smaller letter would lie between copies of a larger letter. A self-pair count is k minus the number of its homogeneous runs. Accordingly every branching factor is <=k-1. In the nontrivial k>=3 equality case, all stages split a fully contiguous block; induction forces the immediately previous largest label to be the only such block and hence fixes the entire maximizing profile. For k=2 all factors equal one. A first split of any block when k>=3 already gives k-1 choices; conversely all-block words give singleton fibers, with n! orders. This covers n=1 as the empty product. The cardinality product, Gamma identity and fixed-k asymptotic give the stated probability. As a cross-check the branching product for any attainable profile reduces to the product over labels of (k-1)!/m_aa!, since a loop branch consumes exactly one loop of its host and only those branches change old loop counts. Independent small multiset-word enumeration rejecting forbidden interlacings directly (not by generating via the supplied insertion routine) verifies that product and the extremal counts, replay: python3 /workspace/review_checks/stirling.py. Finite cases are supplemental; the universal assertions follow from deletion and induction.
